title: A City billing review led a medical provider to agree to withdraw duplicate liens

beats.text: San Francisco found a problem while reviewing workers’ compensation liens.

visual.sub: A review by the self-insured City prompted the investigation

beats.text: The City, which insured itself, referred the matter in March 2020.

visual.kicker: A review by the self-insured City prompted the investigation

beats.text: Investigators compared requests for payment with bills already paid.

visual.kicker: A review by the self-insured City prompted the investigation

beats.text: The district attorney eventually filed 40 insurance fraud charges.

visual.kicker: The original charges and outstanding lien totals describe different things

beats.text: The state counted 3,005 outstanding liens in October 2023.

visual.heading: October 2023 outstanding liens
visual.context: State figures reported by the prosecutor

beats.text: Their face value was more than $29 million.

visual.kicker: The original charges and outstanding lien totals describe different things

beats.text: The filings do not say how much cash was paid twice.
One separate lien ended in an award to the provider.

visual.kicker: Other rulings show why each lien needs its own record

beats.text: In another dispute, the appeals board lacked jurisdiction.
The company later agreed to withdraw the liens identified as duplicate bills.

visual.kicker: The company agreed to withdraw duplicate liens

beats.text: Its February 2026 plea concerned a different statute.

visual.kicker: The company agreed to withdraw duplicate liens

beats.text: The court dismissed the physician’s charges after his death.
The prosecutor also agreed to dismiss the office manager’s charges.

visual.kicker: The company agreed to withdraw duplicate liens

beats.text: The public filings give no total for the duplicate liens withdrawn.
